free_tier.stated: No recurring free allowance. The FAQ reads: 'Is there a permanently free tier? No. The Free Trial is time- and credit-bounded: $5 in credits that expire 30 days after they are granted.' The Free Trial row that carries the eye-catching numbers (gpt-oss-120b and qwen-3.8-27b at 5 RPM, 30K uncached TPM, 90K total TPM, 1M TPH, 1M TPD) sits inside that 30-day, card-gated window, and the same page states 'New accounts receive $5 in free credits after adding a verified payment method.' The trap is that the per-model pages have not caught up: the gpt-oss-120b model page still prints 'Free tier rate limits: 30 requests/min, 60k input tokens/min, 1M tokens/day' as though a free tier existed.

retention.stated: the 30-day credit expiry binds before any rate does: USD 5 at gpt-oss-120b paid output pricing of USD 0.75 per 1M tokens is about 6.7M output tokens in total, or about 3.8M at a 3:1 input-to-output mix, so the whole allowance is one medium batch and not a monthly budget.

record.notes: Corrects the shape of a claim that circulates widely: '1M tokens a day free on Cerebras'. The number is a daily rate limit inside a card-gated 30-day trial, so the monthly figure is not 30M tokens. Arithmetic, labelled estimate: USD 5 / (USD 0.75 per 1M output) = 6.67M output tokens if the credit were spent on output alone; at a 3:1 input-to-output split, USD 5 buys about 3.8M tokens of mixed traffic. The contradiction between the FAQ and the model pages is the real finding for a future reader: a session that reads only the model page records a free tier that the FAQ denies in as many words. See also the SambaNova record in a10-repos, the same pattern of a stale sub-page describing a withdrawn free tier.
